title: Two removals from calcium
statement:
What changes when Ca becomes Ca²⁺?

[_]{a}

choices: Its proton number drops by two.
Its electron count rises by two.
explanations: The outer occupied shell has lower n and electron repulsion is reduced.
Removing the outer shell generally shrinks the ion.
A +2 ion has two fewer electrons.

hints: A positive ion forms by losing electrons.
Losing both 4s electrons removes the outermost occupied shell.
solution: A positive ion forms by losing electrons. Neutral Ca ends in 4s². Losing both 4s electrons removes the outermost occupied shell. The outer occupied shell has lower n and electron repulsion is reduced.
